summary: Iteration 2 regression (reception + patient360 + fixes). Backend 23/23 pytest passing including auth, doctor Next (no 500), booking + Dai Gemini brief, duplicate 400, mine ETA, cancel, reschedule, no-show pushback, done+visit, delay, public queue anonymized, reception dashboard/walk-in, patient360 search/profile/summary, Dai SSE, and WebSocket. Frontend 11/11 flows render: login tabs + Google button, patient Home/Book/Queue + Dai bubble, doctor dashboard with Next & settings, reception dashboard with per-doctor columns + walk-in/call-next, patient360 search page. Role-based TopNav links correct per role. Auth guards verified (patient 403 on doctor queue, non-reception 403 on reception dashboard, invalid Google session returns 401 not 500).

minor.issue: Returns 401 when unauthenticated causing noisy console errors during initial render - cosmetic only, not blocking.
Expects appointment_id as query param (FastAPI treats non-pydantic str as query); likely intended body - works but inconsistent with other POST shapes.
totals.booked never increments because book() creates 'waiting' not 'booked' status; booked column effectively always 0 unless reception uses check-in flow.

issues: Many cancelled rows for same patient (Emily Parker) cluttering Dr. Maya column — recommend filtering cancelled from visible rows or collapsing them.

action_items: Consider hiding cancelled rows from reception column view (purely visual).
Fix reception totals.booked tally — only waiting/called/done appear in rows; 'booked' remains 0 by design but field is misleading.
Suppress /api/auth/me 401 console noise on login screen (frontend can skip the probe when no cookie).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 809 lines — split into routers (auth, appointments, reception, patient360, dai) for maintainability.
generate_brief blocks the booking POST on Gemini streaming (can be 5–20s latency); consider firing async and letting client fetch brief separately.
failed_logins is in-process dict — won't scale beyond single worker and won't persist across restarts.
WebSocket uses global `connections` dict keyed by ws; fine for small scale but no auth and no rate limiting.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_* bookings and one TEST_WalkIn Guest walk-in patient during tests (visible in Dr. Maya column). Safe to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All iteration-2 requirements verified. WebSocket connects and streams initial payload. Reception column may have accumulated TEST walk-ins and many cancelled rows for Emily Parker — if column clutter annoys next tests, run db.appointments.delete_many({status:'cancelled'}) or filter in UI. Previously flagged issues from iter_1 (doctor approval gate, scoped WS broadcast, reschedule endpoint, brute-force lockout) are now fixed in server.py.
